subject: Cost & ops hitlist for MAP and evaluation plan
messages:
From: Emma Yu <emma.yu@helixmed.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: cost sanity + timeline request

Hi Michael / Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to get a short, defensible cost sanity check tied to the MAP so we can confirm budget before end of month (targeting 2026-06-30 for PO). Specifically they want: tokens per session, expected tokens per month, and the major levers (caching, batching, quantization) that move tokens/$ and latency.

We have a rough traffic profile attached (traffic-sample.csv). High-level: ~2k active users/day, ~2 calls per user/day, many short Q&A style interactions (~2-3 turns), and a small cohort (~10% of calls) that do long summaries.

Can Redwood provide:
- A one-page cost sanity with conservative/expected/best-case tokens per $ for the model variant you recommend.
- Any MAP acceptance criteria we should include tied to token consumption and latency (p90/p99).
- A suggested evaluation plan (what to run in our sandbox to validate tokens/$ assumptions).

We need this to feed into procurement and the MAP timeline. Appreciate a quick response today if possible.

—Emma
Emma Yu
Head of ML Platforms, HelixMed

-----Original Attachment: traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 12 KB)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Yu <emma.yu@helixmed.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: cost sanity + timeline request

Emma — thank you, got the sample. Quick read and a few clarifying asks before we produce the one-pager:

1) Are the 2k users "monthly active" or "daily active" in the CSV? (Your note said daily but column names looked like monthly).
2) For the 10% long summaries: what is the average response length (tokens) when you say "long"? Ballpark is fine.
3) Do you expect synchronous UI latency targets (p90/p99) that we should respect for batching tradeoffs?

To set expectations, we will produce a conservative and an optimized estimate. The conservative view assumes: no prefix caching, baseline batching (size ~4), and an n-bit quantized model only if you want us to validate quality. The optimized view assumes a modest prefix cache (20–40% hit on prompt tokens), KV-cache reuse for multi-turns (10–25% token savings on subsequent calls), and batching tuned by latency SLO (8–16 typical).

Karthik will add the technical breakdown (tokens per call, batching/profile assumptions) and Hannah will confirm MAP dates and procurement handoff. I attached a first-pass MAP draft (MAP-draft-v1.pdf) with milestones; we can adjust once we lock token assumptions.

Proposed next steps (today):
- You send quick clarifications above.
- We send a 1-page cost sanity and a short MAP cost acceptance checklist.

Thanks —
Michael Grant
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

-----Attachment: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 84 KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Emma Yu <emma.yu@helixmed.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 14:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: cost sanity + timeline request — technical assumptions

Emma / team — sharing the technical assumptions we typically use for a quick MAP-level sanity. These are conservative but grounded in recent pilots. If you can confirm a few numbers we can finalize the one-pager:

Traffic assumptions (from your CSV, interpreted):
- Active users (daily): 2,000
- Calls per user per day (average): 2 -> 4,000 calls/day
- Average turns per call: 2.5 (prompt + response counted separately)

Token assumptions: (conservative / typical)
- Avg prompt tokens per turn: 220
- Avg response tokens per turn: 200
- Avg tokens per turn total: 420
- Tokenization overhead multiplier: 1.05 (NL -> model tokens)

Monthly projection (baseline, no caching):
- Calls/day: 4,000 -> tokens/day = 4,000 * 420 * 1.05 = ~1.764M tokens/day
- Monthly (30d) = ~52.9M tokens/month

Cost levers (illustrative tokens per $ ranges, model dependent):
- Baseline (floating-point model): ~200k tokens/$1 (higher quality variant)
- Quantized 4-bit variant: ~500k tokens/$1 (roughly 2.5x token/$ improvement vs baseline)

That gives a quick monthly cost ballpark:
- Baseline monthly spend = 52.9M / 200k ≈ $265
- Quantized monthly spend = 52.9M / 500k ≈ $106

Caching & batching impact (conservative estimates):
- Prefix caching: 20–35% reduction on prompt tokens for repetitive prompts
- KV cache reuse for multi-turn: 10–25% savings on subsequent response tokens
- Combined conservative savings: 25% total tokens (end-to-end) -> lowers costs proportionally (e.g., quantized with caching ~ $80/month in above example)

Latency & batching tradeoffs:
- Target p99 <= 600ms: keep batching <= 8 for most interactive routes; use asynchronous batch workers (<=16) for non-interactive (summary) flows.
- If you require p99 <= 300ms, batching must be minimal (~1–2) and cost grows accordingly.

Evaluation plan (short list):
1) Run a 72-hour traffic replay from your sample with
   - raw requests (no caching)
   - with prefix caching enabled at the same hit rates you expect
   - with quantized model variant for quality comparison (A/B)
2) Measure tokens consumed, p50/p90/p99 latency, and quality deltas on a 100-prompt eval set.
3) Share logs for our team to validate the predicted token savings and update the MAP acceptance checklist.

For the MAP doc we should lock: model variant, expected cache hit %, batching plan per route, eval set, and the procurement milestone. If you want, we can run a short sanity replay in our sandbox and give you an "observed tokens/$" number within 48 hours.

—Karthik
Principal Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Yu <emma.yu@helixmed.com>, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, HelixMed Procurement <procurement@helixmed.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: cost sanity + timeline request — next steps and milestones

Hi Emma — thanks for the quick turnaround, and thanks Karthik for the clear breakdown. Short summary and concrete asks so procurement can move: 

Summary (what we'll deliver by EOD PDT):
- 1-page cost sanity (conservative + optimized) with the numeric examples Karthik outlined.
- MAP acceptance checklist focused on tokens per session, caching hit-rate assumptions, and latency SLOs (attached MAP-acceptance-criteria.md).
- A 48-hour sandbox replay offer to observe real tokens consumed (optional, we recommend you accept).

Concrete asks from HelixMed:
1) Confirm whether the 2k in the CSV is daily active (we assumed daily).
2) Provide one representative long-summary prompt (sample text or avg tokens) so we can model that cohort explicitly.
3) Share a 100-prompt eval set (can be synthetic) for quality checks if you want us to validate quantized model outputs.

Procurement timeline: you asked for a PO by 2026-06-30. If we get answers to the 3 asks today, we can finalize the cost sanity + MAP checklist and circulate for signature by 2026-06-17, leaving two weeks for legal/procurement. If procurement needs an internal finance contact, looping in Lauren.

Next internal owners:
- Michael: lead on MAP doc and customer comms
- Karthik: technical validation and replay run
- Lauren: finance/pricing signoff and discounting questions

Emma, please reply with the 3 items above and we'll push the MAP materials to you EOD PST.

Best —
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions | Redwood Inference
